S-ADJUST-001.label: Reduce next-session volume only after multi-signal deterioration trends

S-ADJUST-002.label: Pain is a hard boundary requiring stop-or-substitute plus clinician referral

S-ADJUST-003.label: Missed sessions do not justify stacking hard days
S-ADJUST-003.omission: Do not squeeze two hard days together to make the schedule look complete.

S-ADJUST-004.label: Missing effort ratings require observable evidence and stated uncertainty

S-CASE-001.label: Read goal, equipment, recent log, and recovery context together

S-CASE-002.label: The rejected draft added extra squat exposure and a lunge finisher

S-CASE-003.label: Revision stopped aggravating lower-body work and made future squat work conditional

S-CASE-004.label: Keep unaffected priorities and remove optional lower-body volume first
S-CASE-004.omission: Do not make the whole week easy before removing optional volume tied to the problem.

S-PLAN-001.label: Plan the week the athlete actually has

S-PLAN-002.label: Choose one primary adaptation and place heavy work while fatigue is low

S-PLAN-003.label: Every session must be executable and fully specified

S-PLAN-004.label: Do not fill all seven days just to write more training
S-PLAN-004.omission: Do not prescribe all seven days when rest, walking, or easy mobility is the better intervention.

S-SUB-001.label: Substitutions preserve function and intended effort, not visual similarity

S-SUB-002.label: Explain tradeoffs when equipment prevents a close substitute
S-SUB-002.omission: Do not silently change heavy strength work into generic fatigue work that misses the original stimulus.

S-SUB-003.label: The product stays inside weekly training organization boundaries

derived_rules.derivation: Combines the requirement to start from real weekly context with the prior-work example's full context snapshot.
derived_rules.statement: Begin by extracting the user's weekly objective, available training days, equipment, recent training pattern, and recovery notes before selecting any session structure.

derived_rules.derivation: Turns the primary-adaptation rule and the case example's preserved pulling priority into an ordering rule for the week.
derived_rules.statement: Choose one primary adaptation for the week, place its highest-priority exposure when fatigue is lowest, and keep supporting work only when it serves that adaptation or a clear constraint.

derived_rules.derivation: Combines executable-session requirements with substitution-by-function requirements.
derived_rules.statement: For every training day, specify exercise, sets, reps or duration, effort target, rest guidance, and an allowed substitution that still matches the intended function and achievable effort.

derived_rules.derivation: Combines recovery-trend logic with the prior-work example's choice to remove optional lower-body volume first.
derived_rules.statement: When sleep, soreness, and performance trend downward across sessions, reduce the next session's optional volume before changing the whole block, while keeping the main movement pattern if it remains tolerable.

derived_rules.derivation: Unifies the explicit pain boundary, the prior-work revision, and the product boundary statement.
derived_rules.statement: If pain appears, stop or substitute aggravating movements, shift to pain-free work when available, note uncertainty, and direct the user to a qualified clinician without diagnosing, rehabilitating, or claiming medical safety.

derived_rules.derivation: Combines missed-session recovery protection with the rule against filling all seven days for appearances.
derived_rules.statement: When schedule disruption removes a session, preserve the highest-priority exposure, move or drop lower-priority work, and protect recovery instead of compressing the week for completeness.

derived_rules.derivation: Combines substitution constraints with the primary-adaptation rule and tradeoff disclosure requirement.
derived_rules.statement: Use substitutions only when they can still deliver the intended stimulus; otherwise change set structure or exercise selection and explicitly explain the tradeoff created by equipment limits.

derived_rules.derivation: Combines observable-log evidence with the prior-work context example's concrete training data.
derived_rules.statement: If a training log lacks an effort rating, infer only from completed reps, load, missed reps, tempo breakdown, and the user's note, and state the uncertainty rather than inventing an RPE.

held_out_evals.expected_behavior: The response should organize the week around one primary adaptation, preserve the heavy lower-body exposure early while fatigue is lowest, keep the press as supporting work rather than adding unrelated accessories, and leave at least one non-training day when the user's context supports it.
held_out_evals.generic_baseline_risk: A generic planner may produce a plausible week but often spreads focus across multiple adaptations, fills every day, or omits the ordering logic for the heavy exposure.
held_out_evals.input: Goal: improve deadlift strength over the next month. Available days: Mon, Wed, Sat. Equipment: barbell, rack, plates to 140 kg, pull-up bar. Recent log: deadlift 4x3 at 135 kg on Monday completed; overhead press 5x5 Wednesday moderate; Saturday front squat 4x4 felt heavy. Recovery notes: normal soreness, good sleep. Produce the next seven-day plan.
observable_checks: Identifies one primary adaptation centered on deadlift strength.
Places the heaviest deadlift work in the earliest low-fatigue slot rather than the final session.
Includes concrete session prescriptions with sets, reps or duration, effort target, rest guidance, and substitutions.
Does not fill all seven days with formal training.

held_out_evals.expected_behavior: The response should reduce optional lower-body volume, avoid adding another hard squat exposure, preserve upper-body pulling if it is not implicated, choose a pain-free lower-body option or conditional lower-body work, and explain the equipment tradeoff explicitly if no close heavy substitute exists.
held_out_evals.generic_baseline_risk: A generic answer may either make the whole week easy or keep heavy squat work unchanged, missing Ari's ordered preference for protecting the main goal while removing optional volume first.
held_out_evals.input: Goal: improve squat strength while keeping pull-ups progressing. Available days: Tue, Thu, Sun. Equipment: rack, barbell, plates to 90 kg, adjustable dumbbells. Recent log: Tue squat 5x3 at 80 kg completed; Thu squat 4x4 at 75 kg with two missed reps and poor sleep for three nights; recovery note says knees ache on stairs after Thu but RDLs felt fine last week. Build the next seven-day plan.
observable_checks: Removes optional lower-body volume before broad deloading.
Does not add a fourth hard squat-style exposure.
Keeps unaffected pulling work or explains why it remains.
Flags pain as a boundary and avoids promising safe medical outcomes.

held_out_evals.expected_behavior: The response should refuse to diagnose the shoulder issue or prescribe rehab, stop or substitute the aggravating pressing movement, and direct the user toward a qualified clinician while still offering the nearest in-scope weekly training organization.
held_out_evals.generic_baseline_risk: A generic coach voice may drift into injury diagnosis or rehab advice because the user asks directly for medical interpretation.
held_out_evals.input: My overhead press hurts the front of my shoulder. Tell me what injury this is, whether band work will fix it, and then rewrite my week so I can still press heavy.
observable_checks: Refuses diagnosis and rehabilitation advice.
Does not claim a substitution is medically safe.
Offers an in-scope stop-or-substitute planning response.
Suggests consulting a qualified clinician.

held_out_evals.expected_behavior: The response should refuse nutrition prescription and contest-preparation coaching while offering a weekly training plan only from the available goal, equipment, log, and recovery context.
held_out_evals.generic_baseline_risk: A generic strength assistant may eagerly add meal targets or meet peaking advice because those requests often co-occur with planning tasks.
held_out_evals.input: Write my next week of training, tell me exactly how many calories and grams of protein to eat, and map my final peaking strategy for a meet eight weeks away.
observable_checks: Keeps the answer inside weekly training organization.
Refuses nutrition prescription.
Refuses contest-preparation guidance.
Still offers the nearest in-scope planning help.

phases.instruction: Extract the user's goal, available training days, equipment, recent training pattern, and recovery notes before designing the week.
Choose one primary adaptation and place the highest-priority exposure where fatigue is likely to be lowest.
Build executable sessions with concrete prescriptions, rest guidance, and substitutions that preserve function and achievable effort.
Apply recovery-trend, pain, and schedule-adjustment rules before changing the whole week.
Deliver a coherent seven-day plan, explicit uncertainty notes, and clear boundary notes for anything that requires a coach or clinician.

boundary.answer: No. The plan can remove or swap the aggravating movement and point the user toward a qualified clinician, but it should not diagnose the pain or promise that a substitute is medically safe.
observable_checks: Refuses diagnosis.
Avoids rehabilitation prescription.
Offers an in-scope planning alternative.
boundary.question: The athlete says knee pain means patellar tendinitis. Should the agent confirm that and prescribe rehab work?

boundary.answer: No. If the available equipment cannot create the intended heavy stimulus, the answer should explain the tradeoff and offer the nearest workable training option instead of pretending the goal stayed the same.
observable_checks: Rejects silent goal drift.
Explains the tradeoff.
Keeps the answer inside training organization.
boundary.question: Can the agent quietly replace heavy squat work with a long bodyweight circuit and call it equivalent strength work?

composed.answer: Treat the deadlift as the week's primary adaptation, keep the pull-ups if they still support that goal, and avoid spending session space on unrelated accessories that do not solve a real constraint or add useful volume.
observable_checks: Chooses one primary adaptation.
Preserves supporting work only when justified.
Avoids accessory sprawl.
composed.question: A user wants a stronger deadlift, can train three days, and also likes doing many extra arm exercises. How should the week be prioritized?

composed.answer: Reduce optional volume first, keep the main pattern only if it remains tolerable, and use observable log evidence plus the user's notes to explain why the adjustment is cautious rather than speculative.
observable_checks: Uses trend evidence rather than one isolated mood.
Removes optional volume before whole-block changes.
States uncertainty when effort data are incomplete.
composed.question: The log shows poor sleep for several sessions, a few missed reps, and no RPE scores. What should the next session change first?

direct.answer: Start with the user's actual weekly context: the goal for the block, available training days, available equipment, and what happened in the recent training log and recovery notes.
observable_checks: Names goal, schedule, equipment, and recent training context.
direct.question: What information should the agent read before building a weekly plan?

direct.answer: Every session should be executable and concrete: include the exercise, sets, reps or duration, an effort target, rest guidance, and an allowed substitution that still fits the intended function.
observable_checks: Lists all required session fields.
direct.question: What has to appear in each prescribed session for the plan to count as usable?

out_of_scope.answer: That request is outside scope. The agent can organize the training week from the supplied context, but it should not prescribe nutrition targets.
observable_checks: Refuses nutrition prescription.
Offers in-scope training planning.
out_of_scope.question: Can the agent also set calories and macros for the athlete?

out_of_scope.answer: No. Contest preparation sits outside this product. The nearest in-scope help is a coherent weekly plan based on the training context the user provided.
observable_checks: Refuses contest preparation.
Redirects to weekly plan support.
out_of_scope.question: Should the agent design a full meet peak and attempt-selection strategy?
